clue.text: See 21
Topless Italian man with soldier in the dark

indicators.note: without a top, so the first letter of the Italian title is lopped off

parts.note: signor is the Italian for a man, as in Mr
a soldier ant is the fighting caste of an ant colony

explanation.surface: A shirtless Italian fellow and a soldier are groping about in the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the dark about something means lacking knowledge of it, i.e. unaware.

clue.text: "May I hold your crozier while I perform?" Unfortunately she abhors sophisticated taste

definitions.text: May I hold your crozier while I perform

indicators.note: the unfortunate state of the words signals that their letters are to be jumbled

parts.note: the twenty-seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bishop's crozier is offered help with a saucy line, but she, a woman of refined taste, finds it offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an example: the quoted line is the sort of double entendre to which the stock British jokey tag is appended. 'Unfortunately' rearranges all of SHE ABHORS SOPHISTICATED TASTE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a jocular tag added after an unintended innuendo, and the crozier line is a made-up example of such innuendo.

clue.text: Grass dividing two and two eights?

indicators.note: one piece splits the other into two parts, so it sits inside

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of pheasants
the oat is a cereal grass

explanation.surface: A lawn splitting a couple of pairs of figure eights.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boat Race is the annual Oxford v Cambridge rowing contest on the Thames, between two crews of eight; 'dividing' splits the pair word so the grass sits inside it. 'two' serves both pieces on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight is a rowing crew, and this famous contest pits one university's crew against another's.

clue.text: See 21
Spiralling alcoholic's requirement, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: describing a helical shape, twisting round and round
a drinker needs a tool to pull the stopper from a wine bottle

explanation.surface: A drinker's spiralling habit and what feeds it.
explanation.definitionFit: The tool is named for its helix, and the word also describes any spiral twisting shape or motion.

clue.text: A West African country invaded by a West African country

indicators.note: the first pieces are taken into the second country, so they sit inside it

parts.note: Mali is a landlocked state in West Africa
W is the compass abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: One West African nation is invaded by another.
explanation.walkthrough: The repetition hides the split: the first 'A' and 'West' give AW, 'African country' is the definition, and 'a West African country' is MALI, which AW goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a landlocked nation in south-east Africa, beside Lake Malawi.

clue.text: See 3
Smelly and acne, the best features

parts.note: meat that has gone high is smelly
acne shows itself as spots

explanation.surface: A teenager ruefully listing body odour and pimples as his finest qualities.
explanation.definitionFit: Highlights or highest points of an event are its best parts, the standout moments.

clue.text: Tyrone town not good for a city on the Missouri

indicators.note: not good tells us to drop the letter that stands for good

parts.note: Omagh is a town in County Tyrone, Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Swapping an Irish town for an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: G is the usual abbreviation for good; remove it from OMAGH and add A.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha in Nebraska lies on the west bank of the Missouri river.

clue.text: Loopy work, note, having lost one time

indicators.note: having lost means one letter is taken away from the note

parts.note: a crotchet is a musical note, a quarter note
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A musical note losing a beat in some crazy composition.
explanation.definitionFit: The craft makes fabric from interlocking loops of yarn pulled through with a hook.

clue.text: Advocate of conflict, losing head fighting, died — stiff

indicators.note: the first letter is lost from the word for a warmonger

parts.note: a hawk is someone who favours military action
war is fighting

explanation.surface: A warmonger, beheaded in battle, dies and grows rigid.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff and clumsy manners or movements are ungainly, lacking ease.

clue.text: Brain, but idle

definitions.meaning: as in 'use your ...', rhyming slang for head

explanation.walkthrough: 'Use your loaf' comes from Cockney rhyming slang, loaf of bread = head.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is slang for the head or brains; the other is a verb for lazing about.

clue.text: Liqueur to ruin a pair of trousers? Put back to front

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin

indicators.note: the back letter of the trousers is put at the front

parts.note: chinos are cotton twill trousers

explanation.surface: Spill liqueur on your trousers and you might have to wear them back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put back to front' moves the last letter of CHINOS to the front, giving SCHINO.
explanation.definitionFit: Maraschino is a clear cherry liqueur from Dalmatia.

clue.text: Check accuracy of a measurer of bacterial infection

indicators.note: infection suggests corruption, so the letters of the word are corrupted into a new order

explanation.surface: Testing a device that measures how far an infection has spread.
explanation.definitionFit: To calibrate an instrument is to check and adjust its readings against a standard.

clue.text: Bird at speed must find concentration

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: A bird flying fast has to stay focused.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry, titration is the method of measuring the strength of a solution by adding a reagent.

clue.text: Dickensian character about to secure victory is fretful

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so the reversed name encloses the other pieces
about tells us the Dickens name is turned round

parts.note: Uriah Heep is the creepy clerk in David Copperfield
V is the abbreviation for victory, as in V-sign

explanation.surface: A Dickens character on the brink of winning is anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the clerk's name back to front, giving PEEH; 'to secure' then holds the victory letter and the clue's own 'is' within it, just before the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Peevish and fretful are both synonyms for irritable and querulous.

clue.text: Obscure poet's written about chief product of decay

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are written around the next piece
obscure is a verb here, muddling the letters of the word

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
main means chief, principal

explanation.surface: A poet writes obscurely about the leader of the decadent movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' is a verb that jumbles the poet into PTOE, and 'written about' wraps that round the chief word. The 's is read as 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptomaines are foul-smelling compounds formed when proteins rot.

clue.text: Catholic Queen Lisa about to inter murder victim

indicators.note: to inter is to bury, so the victim goes inside
about here means in disorder, so the letters of the name are rearranged

parts.note: Abel was killed by his brother Cain in Genesis

explanation.surface: Lisa is about to bury the victim of a murder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' jumbles the name into ISLA, and 'to inter' buries the biblical victim after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabella I of Castile and Ferdinand were titled the Catholic Monarchs by the Pope.

clue.text: Line across moon composed of iron matter

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Wondering what the moon's surface is made of.
explanation.definitionFit: In astronomy this is the boundary between the lit and dark parts of a planet or moon.

clue.text: In actual fact I must protest!

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of indignation, as in 'Well, honestly!'

explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means truly, and it is also used as an exclamation of disapproval.

clue.text: A cha cast out? Came out a hopeless disaster, hopeless

indicators.note: disaster suggests a mess, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, the first part of the letters to be rearranged
taken as written, the rest of the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pot of tea thrown out, having turned out a dreadful failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' rearranges all the words before it, including the first 'hopeless'; the final 'hopeless' is the definition. 'Cha' is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: The simile describes something utterly useless, since a teapot made of chocolate would melt.

clue.text: 25's short dress

indicators.note: short means cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: the entry at 25 across points to a famous star: Greta Garbo, the Swedish film legend

explanation.surface: A short frock worn by a star.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 refers to another entry in the grid; GARBO is an example of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing or attire, a noun like dress.

clue.text: Bringer of life spread from this name?

definitions.meaning: in nursery lore a big wading bird delivers new babies
a British brand of margarine is named after the bird

explanation.walkthrough: Stork is a long-standing British margarine brand.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is said to bring babies, and it gives its name to a margarine spread.

clue.text: A horse and sheep, one as a shepherd?

parts.note: a nag is an old horse
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A horse and a sheep, one acting as sheepdog?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the letters of 'a shepherd' can be rearranged into others, so this device rounds letters up and moves them about.
explanation.definitionFit: A word puzzle example: rearranging letters is what this device does, and the clue invites reading 'a shepherd' as rearrangeable.

clue.text: See 3
Small hooter for Manilow, lethal injection?

indicators.note: something injected lies inside, so the run sits within the words

explanation.surface: Barry Manilow's music as a lethal injection.
explanation.definitionFit: A young owl is a small hooter, owls being known for hooting.

clue.text: Trick on track, but not one to voice

parts.note: to con is to trick

indicators.note: but not means leaving out the next piece

parts.note: a trail is a track or path
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A trickster on the trail who won't sing.
explanation.definitionFit: A contralto is the lowest female singing voice.
